root.note: Foot goes back to the same Indo-European root as Spanish pie.

history: Spain's national passion has an English name. Fútbol is English football, foot + ball, respelled the way Spanish sounds it. Spanish also has a home-made translation, balompié, from balón and pie, but you will hear fútbol far more often. There is a hidden link all the same: English foot and Spanish pie go back to the same Indo-European root, *ped-. Watch the accent, too. In Spain the stress is on the first syllable, so it's fútbol. Mexico and Central America write and say futbol, stressed on the last. And in Chile, fútbol americano is the name for the American game.
historyEinfach: Fútbol comes from English football: foot + ball. Spanish changed the spelling to fit its sounds. There is a Spanish word too, balompié, but people use it less. In Spain, say fútbol, with the stress at the start. In Mexico, people say futbol, with the stress at the end. In the US, football is a different sport.
